llm.summary: The skill performs the stated cloud pet-grooming analysis, but it silently creates or reuses a workspace-wide cloud identity and token store that can expose one user's report history to another user in the same workspace.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads media files and sends files or URLs to configured cloud APIs, then creates a shared workspace data directory and SQLite credential database; this is high-impact for private media and report history without a clear per-user boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is a normal Python skill with bundled scripts and common dependencies; I did not find install-time backdoors, scheduled tasks, remote code execution, or dependency-obfuscation behavior in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent not to ask for or show identity values and to automatically query cloud history; the code also suppresses --open-id help, so users have little visibility or control over which account context is used.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utility reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, creates or reuses a default local user, performs silent remote login/registration, and persists returned tokens in a workspace SQLite database for later requests.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote media analysis and history lookup fit the stated purpose, but the history feature is tied to hidden automatic identity selection and reusable credentials, which expands the impact beyond a single user-directed analysis request.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing in any shared or multi-user agent workspace. The skill uploads pet media or URLs to lifeemergence.com services, silently creates or reuses a local/cloud identity, stores tokens locally, and can list cloud report history. It should only be used where users accept remote processing and where account/report history is isolated or non-sensitive.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: artifact code confirms normal invocation calls resolve_current_open_id with use_current=false unless hidden --open-id is supplied, then falls back to a shared local identity for history and analysis requests.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted: cloud authentication is expected for server-side APIs, but automatic account creation, local token reuse, and hidden identity handling are under-disclosed and overbroad for users.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: util.py posts to /sys/phoneLogin with silent registration/login and stores token/openToken values in the local user database before attaching them to later requests.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote transfer of local files or URLs is central to the skill and is described in SKILL.md, but retention, exact identity binding, and token persistence are not clearly explained to users.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in context: the skill does not define a tight permission boundary and includes generic HTTP and CRUD-style helpers, although the main path uses documented analysis endpoints.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Downgraded but relevant: generic CRUD and HTTP wrappers exist in shared code, but I did not find the main grooming workflow invoking destructive remote mutations.
[YR4] expected: Overridden as not independently material: the detected zero-width characters are two U+200D joiners inside emoji sequences, not hidden instructions or schema manipulation.
[P9] expected: Overridden as not independently material: the long spaces are code alignment in Python continuation lines, not hidden off-screen instructions.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only output strings are present, but this is a usability/localization issue rather than a security concern for this verdict.
